_about: Quotes for saints.json, keyed by the Wikipedia article of the saint or celebration. Every quote carries a 'verify' source, and Scripts/enrich_saints.py fetches it and checks the text appears there word for word (ignoring case and punctuation) before the quote reaches the app; a quote that fails is left out. Kinds: 'webc' = the app's bundled World English Bible; 'wikiquote' = the saint's English Wikiquote page; 'url' = a primary text (New Advent's Church Fathers and Summa); Catechism quotes are checked on the Vatican's online Catechism page that holds the paragraph.

Hilary of Poitiers.text: The Son of God is nailed to the cross; but on the cross God conquers human death.

Anthony the Great.text: If we would despise the enemy, our thoughts must always be of God and our souls always glad with hope.
Anthony the Great.source: St. Athanasius, Life of St. Antony

Chair of Saint Peter.text: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.

Feast of Saints Peter and Paul.text: Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

Conversion of Paul the Apostle.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.

Polycarp.text: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?

John Chrysostom.text: Nothing does so much turn our life upside down, as delay and procrastination in the performance of our good works.

Francis de Sales.text: Have patience with every one, but especially with yourself.
Francis de Sales.source: Quoted by Jean-Pierre Camus, The Spirit of St. Francis de Sales

Ignatius of Antioch.text: I am the wheat of God, and let me be ground by the teeth of the wild beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of Christ.

Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows.text: How well the Lord knows how to repay his servants.

verify.wikiquote: Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows

Thomas Aquinas.text: Grace does not destroy nature but perfects it.

Saint Patrick.text: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me.

Benedict of Nursia.text: Listen carefully, my child, to your master's precepts, and incline the ear of your heart.
Benedict of Nursia.source: The Rule of St. Benedict, opening words

Pope Leo I.source: Sermon 21, On the Feast of the Nativity

Catherine of Siena.text: If you are what you should be, you will set the whole world on fire.

Athanasius of Alexandria.text: He was made man that we might be made God.

Saint Monica.text: Lay this body anywhere, let not the care for it trouble you at all. This only I ask, that you will remember me at the Lord's altar, wherever you be.
Saint Monica.source: Her last words, in St. Augustine's Confessions, Book IX

Dominic Savio.text: First I will confess very often and I will receive Communion whenever the confessor gives me permission. Second: I wish to sanctify feastdays. Third: my friends will be Jesus and Mary. Fourth: death but not sins.
Dominic Savio.source: Resolutions on his First Communion, 1849; quoted by Pope John Paul II

Pope Gregory VII.text: I have loved righteousness and hated iniquity, and therefore I die in exile.

Philip Neri.text: A man without prayer is an animal without the use of reason.
Philip Neri.source: Ricordi e Detti di San Filippo Neri

Joan of Arc.text: If I am not in the state of grace, may God put me there; and if I am, may God so keep me.

Anthony of Padua.text: Just as the root feeds the tree, so humility feeds the soul.
Anthony of Padua.source: Sermon for the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost

Nativity of John the Baptist.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

Beheading of John the Baptist.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

Irenaeus.text: The glory of God is a living man; and the life of man consists in beholding God.

Thomas More.text: I die the king's faithful servant, and God's first.
Thomas More.source: St. Thomas More, Words on the scaffold, 1535 (attributed)

Vincent de Paul.text: The reason why God is so great a lover of humility is because He is the great lover of truth; and humility is nothing but truth.
Vincent de Paul.source: As quoted in The Groundwork of the Christian Virtues

Martha.text: Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God's Son, he who comes into the world.

Ignatius of Loyola.text: Take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my understanding, and my entire will.

Jean Vianney.text: The priesthood is the love of the heart of Jesus.
Jean Vianney.source: Quoted in the Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1589

Saint Lawrence.text: The flesh is roasted, turn it and eat.
Saint Lawrence.source: On the gridiron, as told by St. Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy, I.41

Maximilian Kolbe.text: Hate is not a creative force. Love is a creative force.
Maximilian Kolbe.source: Quoted in Saint Maximilian Kolbe: Knight of the Immaculate

Bernard of Clairvaux.text: Believe me, you will find more lessons in the woods than in books. Trees and stones will teach you what you cannot learn from masters.

Bartholomew the Apostle.text: Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!

Augustine of Hippo.text: You have made us for Yourself, and our hearts are restless until they rest in You.

Rose of Lima.text: Apart from the cross there is no other ladder by which we may get to heaven.

Cyprian.text: He can no longer have God for his Father, who has not the Church for his mother.
Cyprian.source: St. Cyprian, On the Unity of the Church, 6

Jerome.text: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.

Saint Remigius.text: Gently bend your neck, Sigamber; worship what you burned; burn what you worshipped.
Saint Remigius.source: At the baptism of Clovis, in Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks, II.31

Thérèse of Lisieux.text: For me, prayer is a surge of the heart; it is a simple look turned toward heaven, it is a cry of recognition and of love, embracing both trial and joy.
Thérèse of Lisieux.source: Story of a Soul; quoted in the Catechism of the Catholic Church, 2558

Francis of Assisi.text: Where there is charity and wisdom, there is neither fear nor ignorance.

Teresa of Ávila.text: Let nothing disturb thee; Let nothing dismay thee: All things pass; God never changes. Patience attains All that it strives for. He who has God Finds he lacks nothing: God alone suffices.
Teresa of Ávila.source: Poem IX, tr. E. Allison Peers

Elizabeth of Hungary.text: Here before my eyes is our sweet Saviour crowned with thorns. My crown would mock Him if I dared kneel at His feet bedecked with gold and jewels.
Elizabeth of Hungary.source: Quoted in Schmidt-Pauli, Elizabeth, Saint of Hungary (1932)

John of the Cross.text: At the evening of life, we shall be judged on our love.
John of the Cross.source: Sayings of Light and Love; quoted in the Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1022

Saint Stephen.text: Lord, don't hold this sin against them!

Thomas Becket.text: For the name of Jesus and the protection of the Church I am ready to embrace death.
Thomas Becket.source: As recorded by Edward Grim, who witnessed his murder

Basil of Caesarea.text: The bread that surpasses you is the bread of the hungry; the tunic hanging in your closet is the tunic of the naked; the shoes you do not wear are the shoes of the barefoot.
Basil of Caesarea.source: St. Basil, quoted by Pope Paul VI, Rinnovamento e Riconciliazione (1976)
